name: Posterior approach to the proximal ulna
aliases: posterior approach to the olecranon and proximal ulna
corridor: Posterior incision curving around the olecranon tip along the subcutaneous ulnar border, exposing the proximal ulna between anconeus and flexor carpi ulnaris while protecting the ulnar nerve

positioning.text: Position with the arm across the chest and the elbow flexed so the posterior elbow and subcutaneous ulna are presented.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the tip of the olecranon and the subcutaneous dorsal border of the ulna.

incision.text: Start a few centimeters proximal to the olecranon tip and curve the incision slightly laterally around the tip to protect the ulnar nerve and avoid a tender scar.

superficial_interval.text: Incise the deep fascia to the dorsal border of the ulna, splitting the triceps tendon to reach the olecranon tip if needed.

deep_interval.text: Expose the proximal ulnar metaphysis between anconeus and flexor carpi ulnaris, extending distally along the subcutaneous ulna as required.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, deep fascia, the triceps tendon, the anconeus and flexor carpi ulnaris interval, and the proximal ulna.

structures_at_risk.text: The ulnar nerve medial to the olecranon is the principal structure at risk.

danger_zones.text: The medial side of the olecranon tip is the danger zone for the ulnar nerve, which is why the incision curves laterally around the tip.

retraction_hazards.text: Keep the ulnar nerve protected medially and avoid a midline scar directly over the olecranon tip.

exposure.text: Exposes the olecranon and proximal ulna, extendable distally as a direct subcutaneous ulnar approach.

limitations.text: It is a posterior ulnar exposure and does not directly address the radial side.

indications.text: Indicated for olecranon and proximal ulnar fractures.

closure.text: Reattach the flexor carpi ulnaris and anconeus, repair the fascia with resorbable sutures, and close subcutaneous tissue and skin.

complications.text: Complications include ulnar neuropathy, a tender posterior scar, and triceps weakness.

procedure_applications.condition: An olecranon or proximal ulnar fracture is fixed posteriorly

questions.question: Why does the incision curve laterally around the olecranon tip?
questions.answer: To protect the ulnar nerve and avoid a tender scar when leaning on the elbow.

questions.question: Between which muscles is the proximal ulnar metaphysis exposed?
questions.answer: Between the anconeus and the flexor carpi ulnaris.

questions.question: How is the approach extended distally?
questions.answer: As a direct subcutaneous approach along the ulnar shaft.
